properties.statement: [BL-177] --check promises a change the real run refuses, and the two give different advice
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-08-02 doing [BL-175].* reflow2_init.py . --check listed update REFLOW2.md; the run then printed REFLOW2.md LEFT ALONE \u2014 differs from what the kit installed (your edits); delete the file to accept the kit copy and changed nothing. Both are individually correct and they disagree, because planned_changes() tests only filecmp.cmp(src, side) \u2014 does the file differ from what the kit ships \u2014 while place_kit_file() additionally tests the manifest hash (*\"the file is ours to refresh only when its current content matches what the kit last installed\"*). A dry run exists to say what a run will do; this one over-promises, and a user who reads --check, runs it, and does not read the full output concludes the update landed. It is worse than a plain mismatch because the remedies differ: --check implies \"run it\", the run says \"delete the file\". Fix shape: planned_changes() applies the same manifest test and reports LEFT ALONE (delete to accept) where the run would \u2014 one predicate, shared, rather than two that drift. Size S", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-177 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S."}
